Natural anti-obesity agents and their therapeutic role in management of obesity: A future trend perspective

Sravani Karri, Sanjay Sharma⁎, Ketan Hatware, Kiran Patil

NMIMS, School of Pharmacy and Technology Management, Shirpur, Maharashtra, India

A R T I C L E I N F O 

Keywords: Obesity Phytoconstituents Mechanism Management Natural products

A B S T R A C T 

In the present scenario, obesity is a challenging health problem and its prevalence along with comorbidities are on the rise around the world. According to world health organization and organisation for economic co-op- eration and development epidemiology reports, overweight and obesity are the fifth foremost causes of deaths globally. The increasing rate of obesity is becoming a mammoth problem which enormously affects an in- dividual’s quality of life. The conventional therapy of obesity mainly involves synthetic moieties and surgical procedures, which has many harmful side effects and chances of recurrence with severity. Hence, the Present review is a metanalysis of all the available data on the use of the plants with their biological source, active phytochemical constituents and a probable mechanism of action as natural anti-obesity agents. The metanalysis of data during the period of 2000–2018 was performed with the help of scientific data search engine National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI/PubMed). This data reveals the need and scope of further research in the development of new natural phytoconstituents for the management of obesity.

Introduction

Obesity is a complex disorder caused by the interaction of numerous genetic, dietary, lifestyle, and environmental factors [1]. The over- weight and obesity are on the rise, around the world. The comorbidities associated with obesity includes diabetes, cardiovascular and locomo- tory diseases. It also has a significant impact on social, financial and psychological status of the individual which may contribute to the de- velopment of depression [2]. In the present era, many conventional drugs are being used for the management of obesity. The availability and harmful side effects of these drugs, limit their utilization. There- fore, there is an utmost need to develop safe, effective and economical entities with easy availability. Plant-derived medicines are considered to be the first line of defence in maintaining health by combating dis- eases and their complications [3]. The effective use of synergistic polyherbal preparations will potentiate the anti-obesity effect by acting on multiple targets. Moreover, these plants are having many health benefits beside its anti-obesity action [4]. Therefore, the use of some plants and there products could be an effective strategy for the man- agement of obesity and associated disorders.

According to the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute guideline of “Pharmacological Management of Obesity”, moderate exercise is one of the best tools along with anti-obesity therapy to overcome

complications of obesity [5]. In the present scenario, researchers fo- cused on the therapeutic potential of natural products against obesity with negligible adverse effects [6]. This review emphasized on the re- cent research work contributed by several researchers across the globe in the field of herbal treatment of obesity. The study includes brief description of the recent trends in epidemiology, pathogenesis and plants along with their phytoconstituents and mechanism of action. Consequently, the country-wise research carried out during 2000–2018 have also discussed.

Among the 7.5 billion population of world, 0.774 billion people were found to be obese, out of which 1.9 million were overweight and 650 million obese [7]. Also, 41 million children under 5 years and 340 million children above 5 years were found overweight or obese in the year 2016 [8]. The three countries USA, China and India have occupied approximately more than 50% obese patients (Fig. 1).

The basic pathogenesis of obesity (Fig. 2) involves either up-reg- ulation of appetite or down-regulation of calorie utilization by gov- erning cellular functions, physical activity etc. This dysregulation is lead to the formation of excess of adipocytes which increases cytokine release, as a result, the vascular complication will arise. These com- plications are associated with hyperlipidemia, cardiovascular abnorm- alities and atherosclerosis.
